name: Oriole Textile Co.
old_description: Established in 1929, Oriole Textile has emerged as a leading wholesaler of fabrics catering to an extensive array of clients worldwide. With over eight decades of experience in the industry, we have honed our expertise in providing superior quality wholesale fabrics to our customers. Our wide range of over 80 high-quality fabrics has earned the trust of discerning clients from various markets and industries. Our clientele encompasses a diverse range of businesses, including fabric stores, bridal shops, dressmakers, party coordinators, florists, event planners, dress manufacturers, and many others. At Oriole Textile, we strive to offer an exceptional customer experience with our extensive product range, competitive pricing, and efficient delivery services. Trust us to be your one-stop-shop for all your wholesale fabric needs.
about:
Oriole Textile Co. operates from New York City’s garment district, where it has been based since its founding in 1929 by Samuel Siegel. The business passed to his son Walter Siegel, then to grandson Mark Siegel, who has led the company for 50 years, and now includes great‑grandson Ron Siegel, making it a fourth‑generation family‑owned enterprise.

The company wholesales more than 80 fabric lines from its showrooms and warehouse, covering categories such as satin, tulle, bengaline, lining, taffeta, poplin, organza, chiffon, crepe, lace, lame, velvet, broadcloth, brocades, knits, sequins, shantung, tricot knits, fire‑retardant fabrics, and prints. It offers color‑card sampling and emphasizes quick order turnaround.

Customers include over‑the‑counter fabric stores, bridal shops, dressmakers, party coordinators, florists, event planners, decorators, bridesmaid manufacturers, and dress manufacturers. The firm serves both small independent shops and larger apparel producers seeking bridal, formal, and party fabrics.

Oriole Textile cites its multi‑generational legacy of honor and integrity, competitive pricing, and exceptional customer service as differentiators. It also highlights a practice of regularly introducing new collections to stay ahead of industry trends.
